 --> Hindustan Copper Q2 net profit jumps 179% to Rs 520 crore on higher metal prices, volumes
 Revenue rises 64 percent to Rs 1,175 crore in September quarter; first-half profit climbs 172 percent to Rs 872 crore as EBITDA margin expands to 60 percent. 
 Moneycontrol News 
 November 12, 2026 / 02:19 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Hindustan Copper Q2 net profit jumps 179% to Rs 520 crore on higher metal prices, volumes HCL net profit surged 179% to Rs 519.54 crore in Q2 FY27.
 Revenue from operations rose 64% to Rs 1,175.24 crore.
 EBITDA margin expanded to 60% driven by higher sales volumes.

 Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) reported a 179 percent year-on-year increase in standalone net profit for the September quarter of FY27, as higher sales volumes and metal prices boosted earnings.
 Net profit for the quarter stood at Rs 519.54 crore, compared with Rs 186.02 crore in the corresponding period last year. Revenue from operations rose 64 percent to Rs 1,175.24 crore from Rs 718.04 crore a year ago, the company said in a press release on November 11.
 Profit before tax surged 180 percent to Rs 695.43 crore from Rs 248.63 crore in the year-ago quarter.
 The company attributed the improvement in profitability to higher volumes and metal prices, supported by operational excellence and sustained productivity.
 The performance came amid elevated but volatile global copper prices. Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) had rallied to record levels in September, with the benchmark cash settlement touching $14,797 a tonne in the second half of the month. Prices remained firm through October, averaging around $14,532 a tonne, before retreating in November.
 The LME cash settlement price fell from $14,675.50 a tonne on October 28 to $13,992 a tonne on November 10, reflecting a correction in the broader metals market. Concerns over demand following a sell-off in technology stocks, alongside shifting expectations around US copper tariffs, contributed to the recent volatility. However, supply constraints and demand from China have continued to provide support to the market.
 For Hindustan Copper, the improvement in earnings was also reflected in its operating margins. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) for the first half stood at Rs 1,268 crore, with the EBITDA margin expanding to 60 percent from 42 percent in the corresponding period last year.
 For the six months ended September 2026, revenue from operations increased 71 percent to Rs 2,111.74 crore from Rs 1,234.41 crore a year earlier. Profit before tax rose 173 percent to Rs 1,167.20 crore, while profit after tax increased 172 percent to Rs 872.15 crore.
 The company, which is India’s only integrated copper producer, has been seeking to expand its mining and production capacity to capitalise on rising demand for the metal from infrastructure, power transmission, electric vehicles and renewable energy.
 Copper is a critical input for these sectors, with demand expected to benefit from electrification and the expansion of power infrastructure. The recent price rally has also improved the earnings environment for miners, although the sharp movements on international exchanges underline the risks to profitability from commodity price fluctuations.
